words: Two 0° plies added to the spar caps from the root to 40 % of the half span, beside the 0° plies: [0/0/0/45/-45/0]s there.

wing.title: Example straight wing
wing.source: An example made for the engine's tests and documents, not a design of ours or of anyone's. Every number is a round value chosen for the example; the material comes from the library.

rules.words: No plies at 90°: each of 0°, +45°, −45° and 90° should have at least 10 %.
rules.source: MIL-HDBK-17-3F, Volume 3, p. 5-69: a laminate carried by its fibers in every direction

rules.words: At most 3 plies of one angle in a row; the limit is 4.
rules.source: MIL-HDBK-17-3F, Volume 3, p. 5-69: plies of one angle together crack apart more easily; thicker plies call for fewer

rules.words: Balanced: every angled ply has a partner at the opposite angle.
rules.source: Laminate theory: a balanced laminate does not shear when stretched (A16 = A26 = 0)
Laminate theory: a symmetric laminate does not bend when stretched (B = 0)

rules.words: No plies at 90°: each of 0°, +45°, −45° and 90° should have at least 10 %.
rules.source: MIL-HDBK-17-3F, Volume 3, p. 5-69: a laminate carried by its fibers in every direction

rules.words: At most 2 plies of one angle in a row; the limit is 4.
rules.source: MIL-HDBK-17-3F, Volume 3, p. 5-69: plies of one angle together crack apart more easily; thicker plies call for fewer

rules.words: Balanced: every angled ply has a partner at the opposite angle.
rules.source: Laminate theory: a balanced laminate does not shear when stretched (A16 = A26 = 0)
Laminate theory: a symmetric laminate does not bend when stretched (B = 0)

rules.words: 2 plies end at 40 % of the span, 1 each side of the middle; at most 2 at one place.
rules.source: MIL-HDBK-17-3F, Volume 3, p. 12-13: plies ending together leave a step where the plies start to part; end a few at a time

rules.words: The plies ending at 40 % of the span need 7.32 mm of run-out at 20 to 1; the thicker side runs 800 mm.
rules.source: MIL-HDBK-17-3F, Volume 3, p. 12-13: a change of thickness tapered over many times its height carries the load past it smoothly

rules.words: The outside ply runs on over the plies ending at 40 % of the span (ply 3 of the inboard half stack).
rules.source: MIL-HDBK-17-3F, Volume 3, p. 12-12: a ply that runs on over the ends of the dropped plies holds them down
